newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: AUSTRALIA'S FISCHER URGES BANKS TO CUT LOAN RATES.
newsitem.headline: AUSTRALIA'S FISCHER URGES BANKS TO CUT LOAN RATES.

text.p: Australian acting Prime Minister Tim Fischer on Thursday urged banks to cut interest rates for all borrowers' loans and expressed concern about rising bank fees.
"The major banks have not only failed to pass on (official) interest rate reductions in full to lenders but also appear to continually raft up bank fees and charges," Fischer told reporters.
"We want from the banks a better deal in this regard to assist the rebuild of the economy," Fischer said.
"Interest rate cuts alone are not going to light up comprehensively the economy, I recognise that, but the passing on of those interest rate reductions will greatly help."

Fischer said banks were charging 15 percent to 20 percent from some business loans, which was "clearly absolutely unacceptable at a circumstance where this federal government in its first 500 days of office has delivered ... five consecutive half percent interest rate cuts".

"What we need to do is see that the competition ripples right through to the coalface across country Australia and further that the banks and their habits are exposed and the due authorities and tribunals deal with it where there is scope for doing just that."
"The Reserve Bank has officially found the major banks have conssitently lagged the alterations downward in interest rates.
"But if you go in the other direction, have increases in interest rates, they jump in a whole lot more quickly."
The Liberal-National government has consistently criticised banks for not passing on the full effect of cuts to official interest rates.
The Reserve Bank has made five 50 basis point reductions in official cash rates, the most recent on July 30 bringing official rates down to 5.0 percent.
